record_under_review.evidence_span: PLENA targets long-context agentic LLM inference, where large DOMs and tool-call trajectories create bandwidth and capacity memory walls. It combines hardware supporting asymmetric quantization, a flattened systolic array with native FlashAttention support, and a full stack with custom ISA, compiler, cycle-emulated simulator, and automated design-space exploration. Simulated results report up to 8.5x higher utilization than existing accelerators, 2.24x higher throughput than an A100, and 3.85x higher throughput than a TPU v6e under matched multiplier and memory settings; the system is intended for open-source release.
record_under_review.hardware_or_process_assumptions: Custom accelerator with flattened systolic array, asymmetric quantization, custom ISA/compiler, and cycle-emulated simulation; reported gains are simulated and depend on matched hardware-resource assumptions.

record_under_review.problem: Long-context agentic LLM inference generates large off-chip memory traffic from extended web, tool, and interaction histories, creating simultaneous bandwidth and capacity memory walls that leave compute units underutilized.
record_under_review.title: Combating the Memory Walls: Optimization Pathways for Long-Context Agentic LLM Inference
record_under_review.workload_or_benchmark: Long-context agentic LLM inference involving web or computer-use inputs, tool-call trajectories, and extended contexts; evaluation uses simulated accelerator execution and matched multiplier/memory settings against A100 and TPU v6e references.
